text: Việt Nam seeks to build homegrown e-commerce platforms to compete with Shopee and TikTok Shop

HÀ NỘI - Việt Nam aims to establish one to two strong e-commerce platforms capable of competing with Shopee and TikTok Shop by 2030, according to a draft proposal on the development of Việt Nam's e-commerce ecosystem to 2035.

Under the proposal, by 2030 the Ministry of Industry and Trade (MoIT) aims to develop one to two competitive e-commerce platforms owned and operated by Vietnamese businesses, with a strong presence in the domestic market.
The country aims to have two to three such platforms capable of competing in the domestic market by 2035.
In addition, the proposal aims for at least 50 per cent of suppliers to meet the basic requirements for conducting business on e-commerce platforms by 2030, rising to 60 per cent by 2035.
It also targets at least 50 per cent of suppliers generating transactions after being connected to the market by 2030, increasing to 60 per cent by 2035.

Targets have been set for the proportion of enterprises and cooperatives participating in cross-border e-commerce and generating transactions with overseas markets to be at least 40 per cent by 2030 and 60 per cent by 2035.

The proportion of business models with mechanisms for information sharing and clear accountability among sellers, platforms and service providers in handling feedback, complaints, returns and refunds is expected to reach at least 50 per cent by 2030 and 80 per cent by 2035.

Việt Nam's e-commerce market was valued at approximately US$31 billion last year, representing annual growth of around 25 per cent and accounting for approximately 11 per cent of the country's total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue, according to the MoIT.
Around 60 per cent of the population participated in online shopping.

The MoIT also estimated that total sales across four platforms - Shopee, TikTok Shop, Lazada and Tiki - reached approximately VNĐ429.7 trillion ($16.8 billion) last year, accounting for around 68 per cent of total sales in Việt Nam's domestic e-commerce market.
Of this figure, Shopee accounted for nearly 51.2 per cent and TikTok Shop for 46.5 per cent.
Together, the two platforms represented approximately 97.6 per cent of the combined sales of the four platforms surveyed.

This market concentration highlights the need for policies to support the development of several strong e-commerce platforms that can compete in the domestic market and are owned and operated by Vietnamese businesses.

To achieve these targets, the MoIT has also outlined a range of solutions and assigned implementation responsibilities to relevant agencies and organisations, with the aim of building a developed, trusted and efficient e-commerce ecosystem. - VNS
